I got the script for Macbeth from Gutenburg

```{python}
import re
import pandas as pd
```
```{python}
# Stopwords (from Day 18)
stopwords = ["the", "to", "and", "of", "a", "her", "i", "in", "was", "it",
             "she", "he", "be", "that", "you", "not", "had", "as", "his", "for",
             "with", "is", "have", "but", "at", "so", "all", "my", "been", "him",
             "on", "by", "could", "would", "very", "no", "what", "which", "they",
             "were", "there", "me", "an", "must", "this", "said", "from", "or",
             "will", "any", "much", "than", "such", "their", "them", "if", "do",
             "did", "one", "when", "your", "more", "are", "we", "who", "up",
             "out", "down", "into", "s", "t"]
```
```{python}
with open("../../homework/hw5/hwf_raw.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    macbeth_lines = f.readlines()

while not macbeth_lines[0].startswith("*** START"):
    macbeth_lines = macbeth_lines[1:]
macbeth_lines =macbeth_lines[1:]

while not macbeth_lines[-1].startswith("*** END"):
    macbeth_lines = macbeth_lines[:-1]
macbeth_lines = macbeth_lines[:-1]

macbeth_text = "".join(macbeth_lines)
```
```{python}
chapters = re.split(r"\nCHAPTER [IVXL]+", macbeth_text)
chapters = chapters[1:]
```
```{python}
# 3. One row per word, with its chapter
rows = []
chapter_num = 0

for chapter in chapters:
    chapter_num += 1
    words = re.split(r"[\W_]+", chapter.lower())   # split on \W AND on _
    words = [w for w in words if w != ""]
    for w in words:
        rows.append({"word": w, "chapter": chapter_num})

macbeth_df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
```
```{python}
# 4. Save it for next time
macbeth_df.to_csv("macbeth_words.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8-sig")
```

#3. 1: 67, 2:66 , 3: 60, 4: 96, 5: 64, 6: 90, 7: 83, 8: 101, 9: 63, 10: 60, 11: 68, 12: 101

```{python}
queen_by_chapter = {}

for w, ch in zip(alice_df["word"], alice_df["chapter"]):
    if w == "queen":
        if ch in queen_by_chapter:
            queen_by_chapter[ch] += 1
        else:
            queen_by_chapter[ch] = 1

print(queen_by_chapter)
```
